The facilitator picks **one paper of at most 15 pages**, guided by the two core criteria below, and announces it to all GEOTEC members **at least one week before the session**.

## Core criteria

Every selected paper should meet **both** criteria:

| Criterion | What to look for |
|:----------|:-----------------|
| **Relevance to the group** | A clear link to GIScience; topic, method or data of interest to several GEOTEC members, not only the facilitator |
| **Methodological interest** | A method, design or validation approach worth dissecting, even outside members' own topics |

: Core selection criteria {#tbl-criteria}

::: {.callout-tip}
## Why these criteria?
Because the club trains critical reading rather than keeping up with a topic, a paper with rich methods or instructive writing is a better pick than one that is merely new or close to your own thesis.
:::

## Practical requirements

- [ ] Maximum 15 pages (excluding references and appendices)
- [ ] Accessible to all members: open access, or a PDF shared with everyone
- [ ] Readable by non-specialists in the group with reasonable effort
- [ ] Not already discussed in a previous session (check the archive)

## Occasional picks

- Classic or landmark papers that everyone should know
- Recent preprints
- Controversial papers, which often teach the most about critical reading and debate

## Announcement

At least one week before the session, the facilitator sends the following to all members (Geoinfo mailing list):

1. Full reference and DOI or link to the PDF
2. One or two sentences on why this paper was chosen
3. A reminder to bring one question or critique, using the shared guiding questions, to the session

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Announcement email template

> **Subject:** GEOTEC Journal Club – *session date* – *Paper title*
>
> Dear all,
>
> For our next Journal Club session (*date, time, room*), we will discuss:
>
> *Author(s) (Year). Title. Journal. DOI/link*
>
> **Why this paper:** *one or two sentences.*
>
> Please read it before the session and bring one question or critique, using the shared guiding questions.
>
> *Facilitator name*
:::
